steps.body: Drawing a shape is making its rules with a pencil: straight sides, real corners, and an outline that closes back home.
steps.narration: Drawing a shape is making its rules with a pencil: straight sides, real corners, and an outline that closes back home.

widget.prompt: Measure the short drawn side. Start at zero and cover it with 3 equal unit blocks.
widget.successFeedback: 3 equal blocks cover the short drawn side exactly.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: Three straight strokes, but the ends miss. A triangle yet?
predict.reveal: The outline must return to its start; a gap leaks the inside out.

cml.actionGoal: Name shapes by sides and corners, place them with position words, and compose them edge to edge for kgb draw shape.
invariants: A shape's name lives in its sides and corners — not its size, pose, or color; position words compare a thing to a landmark; and shapes joined edge to edge compose a larger whole — the anchors for kgb draw shape.
misconceptions: Renaming a turned or resized shape, using position words without a landmark, or treating shapes as unjoinable.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the shape were turned upside down, which of its sides or corners would disappear?

widget.prompt: Drawing a triangle — what must the pencil do?

options.label: Draw one long curved line
options.feedback: Curves make circles and blobs; the triangle asks for straight sides only.

options.label: Draw 3 straight sides that close
options.feedback: Correct — three straight strokes, each ending where the next begins, the last returning home to close it.

options.label: Draw exactly 3 dots
options.feedback: Dots mark where corners WILL be; the sides between them make the shape.

options.label: Draw 4 straight sides
options.feedback: A fourth side builds a quadrilateral; the triangle closes after three.

widget.prompt: A drawing has 3 straight sides but a gap where the ends miss. Is it a triangle?

options.label: Yes — three sides alone is enough
options.feedback: Three sides that fail to meet leave an open path, not a shape.

options.label: Yes, even if the gap is small
options.feedback: Small or large, a gap breaks the closed outline that defines the shape.

options.label: Not yet — it must close all the way around
options.feedback: Correct — the outline must return to its start; a gap leaks the inside out and unmakes the shape.

options.label: No drawing is ever a triangle
options.feedback: Close the gap and the drawing becomes a perfectly good triangle.

widget.prompt: Count the strokes: start at 3 and count on 3. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: That stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 6.
That goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 3 hops from 3.

widget.missFeedback: Count 3 on from 3: you land on 6.
widget.successFeedback: 6 — each stroke takes one hop, and the landing is the count.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 3 counts are needed to reach 6.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count stops after 3 hops, on 6.

widget.prompt: Which drawing follows every rule for a triangle?

options.label: 3 straight sides that close
options.feedback: Yes. Three straight sides meet end to end and close the triangle.

options.label: 3 straight sides with a gap
options.feedback: The gap leaves the outline open. Join the ends to finish the triangle.

options.label: 2 straight sides that meet
options.feedback: Two sides cannot close a flat shape. A triangle needs 3.

options.label: 1 curved line that closes
options.feedback: A curved outline can make a round shape, but a triangle needs straight sides.
